messages:
ellen: Heads up — noticed a flurry of NVMe read/write errors on gnode-14 (rack 7) right when a batch of GPU instances were provisioning. GPUs stayed in PROVISIONING for ~4-6m.
raj: any core logs or kernel oops?
ellen: pasted kernel dmesg snippet: ```nvme0n1: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 2345234
blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 2345234 op 0x1:(WRITE) flags 0x0 phys_seg 1 prio 0
```
matt: hmm, those look like write requeue errors. Did the ephemeral-cleaner run?
infra-bot: alert posted to #incidents: nvme_io_error on gnode-14 — 12 events in 2m (severity: warning)
ellen: cleaner started a scrub at 03:10 UTC (scheduled maintenance window) and we saw a fingerprint mismatch during background verify -> scrub retried chunks which drove write amplification.
carla: fingerprint mismatch? that's unusual. which layer reported it? fstrim/overlay?
matt: overlay snapshot integrity check flagged 3 blocks as changed vs expected, cleaner rehydrated them which created lots of small writes. Our nvme queue depth + background GC couldn't keep up.
raj: so two issues: (1) scrub retries -> high write IOPS, (2) drive starting to show SMART errors leading to retries. Need to rate-limit scrub and drain node.
ellen: I paused the cleaner for gnode-14 with the quick action: ```/usr/local/bin/cleanerctl pause --node gnode-14 --reason "io-spike"```
ellen: provisioning cleared after pause, latency back to normal.
kyra-oncall: thanks. can we avoid cross-node rescheduling thrash? we had 8 GPU jobs requeued.
matt: short-term mitigation: set cleaner concurrency to 1 for that AZ and enable scrub-throttle: ```/etc/cleaner/conf.d/limits.yaml:
  max_parallel_scrubs: 1
  scrub_io_limit_iops: 1200```
carla: longer-term: schedule RMA for device in slot 3 on gnode-14. SMART shows increasing "media_errors" and "prog_fail_cnt".
raj: also file a follow-up to evaluate our fingerprint false-positive rate — could be a checksum drift from async snapshot rebase. Ticket: INFRA-2147.
ellen: cost note — this reroute/drain bumped GPU startup times ~+6m and caused ~0.4 GPU-hours wasted on restart churn. Moving to dedicated batch windows might help.
kyra-oncall: assigned to matt for rolling cleanup plan + RMA coordination, raj to own fingerprint root-cause. I'll add incident tag and inform SRE rotation.
matt: I'll run a small canary patch to cleaner to implement exponential backoff on retries and land in next deploy.
ellen: leaving node in paused-cleaner state and tagging as "drain-pending". Will kick off kube cordon/drain at 04:30 UTC after we confirm replacement slot.
carla: ordered RMA, ETA 2 business days.
raj: adding note: if we see similar spikes in us-west-2 within 24h, widen throttle globally and enable per-node scrub-rate limits.
ellen: thanks team :thumbsup:
kyra-oncall: closing loop — updated incident INFRA-2147 with logs, SMART export, and mitigation steps. Keep updates in this thread.
